title: Disposition of the seven unwired files in the census's rank-2 governed-risk directory
method: Every verdict below is measured on the base commit, not read from an earlier record. Two earlier verdicts were checked against the file as it stands and one of them had gone stale.

sourceTextScanner is counted, not asserted: readFileSyncCount is occurrences of readFileSync in the file and toContainCount is occurrences of toContain(. A file that reads source at module scope and asserts substrings of it is a scanner however green it runs.

collected: false was settled by running each file directly BEFORE judging it. A file Jest cannot parse and a file Jest never reaches are indistinguishable in the census, and only the first is breakage.
The two render modes of workspace-explicit-client-api-routing are two files. One collecting says nothing about the other, and here they take opposite verdicts.
The repository's standing rule, from the T-742 guard, is that a source-text scanner cannot be wired into CI. Four of these seven are held unwired by it.

suites.rationale: T-550 verdicted this rewrite_as_behavior and the verdict was CORRECT at its declared base 05bdab64e, where the file held 1 readFileSync and 16 toContain against WorkspaceClient.tsx. b66e4cd22 (#8201, 'assert Source route behaviour instead of file bytes') rewrote it +248/-53 and is NOT an ancestor of that base, so the rewrite the verdict asked for was delivered on a parallel line and nobody amended the record. Measured here: 0 readFileSync, 0 toContain, dependencies mocked, component mounted, 6 cases green. T-553's premise is discharged; the T-550 record is left as the historical draw it is.

T-742 already verdicted this wire_into_ci with sourceTextScanner false and T-743 owned the wiring, which had not happened. Re-measured rather than taken on trust: 0 readFileSync, 0 toContain, renders, 3 cases green. Wired. Its .test.ts sibling takes the opposite verdict below.

Already collected and covered, but reached only from COMMAND_CHECKS in scripts/ecl/run_product_ecl_predeploy_gate.mjs, whose only caller is ecl-product-live-proof.yml, triggered by workflow_dispatch and by workflow_run after 'ACA main deploy' — neither pull_request nor merge_group. It ran green AFTER the deploy it might have stopped. Its 30 toContain assert values produced by the adapter against mocked reads and a real temporary directory, not the bytes of a source file, so it is not a scanner. Wired into a merge-blocking step in addition to the pre-deploy gate, which keeps its own invocation.

T-556 verdicted this rewrite_as_behavior because it reads source files at module scope and asserts substrings, so a comment carrying the same substring satisfies every case. Re-measured on this commit rather than assumed: still 1 readFileSync and 5 toContain, still renders nothing. The verdict stands and T-558 owns the rewrite. Wiring it would buy a green check and no protection.

quarantineEntry.why: The CI coverage census credits a file as triaged only when a command subtracts it or a scoped scripts/quality/*-quarantine.json declares it. This verdict alone left the file reading as untriaged. The list entry declares the hold where the census reads, and its checker re-measures this rationale rather than believing it: when the suite stops reading source text the entry fails, so it cannot outlive its reason.

suites.rationale: DISCHARGED by T-764. The held_unwired verdict was correct at this record's base: the file was a source-text scanner (6 readFileSync, 100 toContain) and the repository's rule forbids making one merge-blocking. T-764 removed the reason rather than waiving it. The file now calls SourceWorkspacePage with real searchParams, mounts the tree it returns with the real WorkspaceClientLoader and the real WorkspaceClient beneath it, and reads the client parameter off the contract-detail request those components actually made: 14 cases, 0 readFileSync calls, and one toContain left in the file, which asserts rendered DOM text rather than the bytes of a source file (toContainAgainstSourceTextCount 0). The header prose was also reworded to stop naming those two tokens: a line describing the defect was itself an instance of it under a token grep. Calibrated in both directions before wiring. With the tenant membership fence still running and its call text byte-identical, only its verdict ignored, the old scanner passed 13 of 13 and the rewrite fails 4 of 14; on a behaviour-preserving rename of a local binding the old scanner failed 1 of 13 and the rewrite passes 14 of 14. Wired into .github/workflows/unit-suites.yml beside portfolioAdapter.ecl.test.ts; removing that one path drops pullRequestCoveredTestFiles 1998 -> 1997, and the per-file record flips pullRequestCovered false -> true with via gaining 'command'. The pre-deploy ECL gate keeps its own invocation.
suites.priorVerdictRationale: NEW FINDING, and the reason this item does not simply wire the second half. It shares portfolioAdapter.ecl.test.ts's defect — reached only from the post-deploy ECL gate, so nothing it asserts can block a merge — but it is also the heaviest source-text scanner of the seven: 6 readFileSync and 100 toContain. The repository's own rule forbids wiring a scanner into CI, so making it merge-blocking would convert an unenforced check into an enforced check of source bytes. It needs a behavioural rewrite and has no owner; filed back to the backlog rather than wired or deleted here.
suites.reverificationCondition: This entry asserts the file executes the route rather than reading its bytes. The measure is toContainAgainstSourceTextCount and readFileSyncCount, not the raw toContain count: one toContain is expected and legitimate, against rendered DOM text. If any readFileSync call appears, if any assertion is made against the contents of a source file, or if rendersComponent becomes false, the wiring is no longer justified by this rationale and the verdict must be re-taken.

amendments.why: The verdict's stated reason was that the file was a source-text scanner. T-764 rewrote it to execute the route, so the reason no longer holds. Recorded as a discharge rather than a deletion: the prior verdict and its rationale are kept in priorVerdict and priorVerdictRationale. Counts corrected before merge: an earlier draft of this entry recorded readFileSyncCount 0 and toContainCount 0, which was wrong as a literal token count — the header prose named both tokens and two assertions used toContain. The prose was reworded, one assertion was tightened from a substring of the request pathname to an exact match, and the remaining one is recorded rather than rounded away.

amendments.change: held_unwired verdicts now require a scoped quarantine entry
amendments.why: Measured before choosing a mechanism: of the 395 repo-wide untriagedUnrunTestFiles on 31f6badae, 20 already carried a verdict in some docs/architecture/*triage*.json and 375 carried none; of those 20 only these 3 carried a verdict that declares a HOLD, the other 17 carrying wire_into_ci, repair, update_with_reason_recorded, vacuous_control_proof or real — every one of which means work is owed. Teaching the census to read triage records would have had to credit those 17 too, which subtracts queued work from the ranking that decides what gets wired next. So the census vocabulary is unchanged and the hold is declared where the census already reads. scripts/quality/check-source-workspace-quarantine.mjs enforces both directions: a held_unwired verdict anywhere in the tree with no entry fails, and an entry whose record no longer carries the verdict fails.
